notes: Rule: A.1 182) 'SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause (coded character set referenced by STANDARD-2 phrase). This item is required. This item shall be documented' (cite.py --check A.1 'coded character set referenced by STANDARD-2 phrase' -> OK §A.1 182). §12.3.7.4 GR7 c: 'When the STANDARD-2 phrase is specified, the referenced coded character set shall be as specified in ISO/IEC 646; the implementor shall specify whether the International Reference Version or a national version is referenced, and shall specify the circumstances that define which national version is referenced' (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 -> OK §12.3.7.4 7) c). CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-182 |' row in §7 (grep; inventory GAP). The answer IS written, unkeyed: §2 row 27 (CODE-SET) says 'STANDARD-1/STANDARD-2 (ISO/IEC 646 IRV — the native set's first 128 characters ...)', and the CodedCharacterSet summary in CollatingModel.cs states 'STANDARD-1 / STANDARD-2 are ISO/IEC 646 IRV, 128 characters'. Code fixes exactly that: STANDARD-2 always = IRV, never a national version (so the 'circumstances' half is vacuous but is not stated as such); CollatingModel normalizes it to the identity sequence and CobolClass.CodedSetKind.Ascii gives it the 128-character membership. Probe s2.cob at pin (--std 85 and 2023): ALPHABET S2 IS STANDARD-2 as PCS; 'AB~' IS S2 true, 'é' IS S2 false, ORD('A')=66, 'a'>'B', 'é'>'~' — IRV + native order, matching the prose. PARTIAL (the wave-1 DOC-A.1-94 shape): determination made and written, but not filed under its own key, so audit_annex_a1.py counts it open and nothing pins it — pb109/pb110 goldens exercise STANDARD-1 only, never STANDARD-2. Editions: STANDARD-2 in every edition (reserved-words table 'continuous since 1985'). Owning notes: umbrella register backlog kb/Work/A11 and kb/Work/PB160 (open); no item-specific note found (grep item 182 / DOC-A.1-182 in kb/Work: none).

Rule: A.1 187) 'SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause, STANDARD-1 and STANDARD-2 phrases (correspondence with native character set). This item is required. This item shall be documented' (cite.py --check A.1 'STANDARD-1 and STANDARD-2 phrases (correspondence with native character set)' -> OK §A.1 187). §12.3.7.4 GR7 c: 'Each character of the standard character set is associated with its corresponding character of the native alphanumeric character set. The implementor defines the correspondence between the characters of the standard character set and the characters of the native character set.' (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 -> OK §12.3.7.4 7) c). CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-187 |' row in §7. The correspondence IS stated, unkeyed, in §2 row 27 ('ISO/IEC 646 IRV — the native set's first 128 characters, so the §12.3.7.4 GR7 c correspondence is the identity') and in the DOC-A.1-183 cell ('the first 128 positions of the native alphanumeric character set ARE ISO/IEC 646 IRV'). Code: identity on U+0000-U+007F (CollatingModel identity alphabet; CobolClass.CodedSetKind.Ascii; CODE-SET STANDARD-1/-2 converts as identity). Probe s2.cob at pin: STANDARD-1 and STANDARD-2 both exclude 'é', include 'AB~', ORD/compare native. Pinned for STANDARD-1 only by conformance:2023/pb109_class_condition_alphabet and conformance:2023/pb110_code_set_identity (neither uses STANDARD-2, and neither is a DOC row test-ref). PARTIAL: determination made, correct and written, but not filed under its own §7 key and no witness names the item. Editions: all four. Owning notes: kb/Work/A11, kb/Work/PB160 (register backlog, open); no item-specific note.

Rule: A.1 186) 'SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause, literal phrase (ordinal number of characters not specified). This item is required. The implementor shall document the scheme used for assigning the ordinal number, but does not need to specify the ordinal number character-by-character.' (cite.py --check A.1 'The implementor shall document the scheme used for assigning the ordinal number' -> OK §A.1 186). §12.3.7.4 GR7 k 4.: 'If a character code set is being specified, the implementor defines the ordinal number within the character code set being specified for each character within the native character set that is not specified by the literal-1 phrase.' (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 -> OK §12.3.7.4 7) ... 4.). CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-186 |' row, and §2 row 27 says the opposite ('a literal-phrase alphabet's remapped ordinals (GR7 k4 leaves that correspondence to the implementor and this one does not define it)'), while the CollatingModel CodedCharacterSet summary claims the scheme is 'documented in CONFORMANCE.md'. Code FIXES a scheme: ordinal = collating position + 1, unspecified native characters following the highest specified position in native relative order (CharAt's sparse GR7 k3 inverse). Probe k4.cob at pin: ALPHABET AL IS "Z" "Y" "X"; SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS S1 S4 S5 ARE 1 4 5 IN AL -> S1='Z', S4=U+0000, S5=U+0001 (the first unspecified native chars). Fixed-but-undocumented (and mis-documented) determination = DIVERGES, harm silent. OWNING NOTE: kb/Work/PB1092 (open, MINOR) names item 186 and this exact mechanism in its title — cited, not re-reported. Editions: literal-phrase ALPHABET exists in all four.

Rule: A.1 192) 'STOP and GOBACK statements (constraints on the value of the STATUS literal or on the contents of the data item referenced by the STATUS identifier). This item is required. This item shall be documented' -> §14.9.42.4 GR5 'Any constraints on the value of literal-1 or the contents of the data item referenced by identifier-1 are defined by the implementor.' (cite.py --check 14.9.42.4 -> OK §14.9.42.4 5)); §14.9.18.4 GR10 twin (cite.py --check 14.9.18.4 -> OK §14.9.18.4 10)). CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-192 |' row in §7; the determination IS written in the §3 bullet 'STOP RUN / GOBACK termination status (... Annex A required items 192/193)': integer value -> exit code; non-numeric operand digit-decoded (CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric), all-non-digit -> 0; figurative/ALL/boolean/national/hex forms enumerated; NULL rejected COBOLNET1704; long narrowed to Int32 and POSIX low-8-bit clamp. Probes at pin (st.cob, --run exit code): NORMAL STATUS 300 -> 44, ERROR STATUS -3 -> 253, ERROR STATUS 4294967296 -> 0, ERROR STATUS "ABEND" -> 0, NORMAL STATUS 7 -> 7, STATUS 2.7 -> COBOLNET1704 — all as the prose states. Pinned by StopGobackExitCodeTests (TerminationStatus_SetsProcessExitCode, NonNumericStatusOperand_IsLegalAndInterpretedNumerically, and the figurative/ALL/boolean theory). PARTIAL because (a) the determination is not filed under its own §7 key (audit counts item 192 open — the wave-1 DOC-A.1-94 GOBACK sibling shape), and (b) its 'GR5 value overrides GR2' precedence (ERROR STATUS 0 / "ABEND" / 4294967296 exits 0, i.e. an ERROR termination reported as normal) is contested by kb/Work/PB1178 (open, MAJOR, owner-visibility) — cited, not re-reported. Editions: STATUS phrase on STOP/GOBACK is 2002+ syntax (STOP RUN WITH ... STATUS absent from 85). Umbrella register note kb/Work/A11.

Rule: A.1 193) 'STOP and GOBACK statements (mechanism for error termination). This item is optional. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented' -> §14.9.42.4 GR4 'If neither the ERROR phrase nor the NORMAL phrase is specified, the operating system will indicate a normal termination of the run unit ... unless error termination has been indicated by an implementor-defined mechanism.' (cite.py --check 14.9.42.4 -> OK §14.9.42.4 4)); §14.9.18.4 GR9 twin (cite.py --check 14.9.18.4 -> OK §14.9.18.4 9)). CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-193 |' row. The §3 'STOP RUN / GOBACK termination status' bullet labels an 'item 193' paragraph, but what it states under that label is the GR2/GR3 ERROR/NORMAL phrase mapping (ERROR with no value -> 1, NORMAL/no phrase -> 0) — not the GR4/GR9 question. The answer to GR4 is only implicit: 'Programs with no status phrase leave the exit code at 0' — i.e. NO implementor mechanism is provided (there is no RETURN-CODE special register: probe rc.cob 'MOVE 5 TO RETURN-CODE' -> COBOLNET1639 at 85 and 2023; the only nonzero exit without a phrase is abnormal termination on a fatal EC, item 44, which is not a STOP/GOBACK). Behaviour at pin agrees: 'STOP RUN.' and 'GOBACK.' exit 0 (StopGobackExitCodeTests.TerminationStatus_SetsProcessExitCode regression lock). PARTIAL: behaviour consistent, but the optional item should read 'Not provided.' under its own §7 key (PB280 Q1 rule) so the a1-optional-not-provided selector can reach it; today the prose mislabels a GR2 mapping as item 193 and the inventory row stays GAP. Editions: GR4's STOP RUN without phrase exists in all editions (the phrase rules 2002+). Owning notes: kb/Work/A11, kb/Work/PB280 (the Not-provided convention); PB1178 (open) covers the adjacent ERROR/value precedence.
